claims.text: Near-equiatomic FeCoNi can exist as a single-phase FCC alloy.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase FCC FeCoNi has coercivity of approximately 100 Oe or lower.
Controlled annealing can induce limited nanoscale precipitation of an ordered phase in FeCoNi.
The annealing temperature and duration can be tuned to control nanoscale precipitation.
Annealing can produce ordered B2 precipitates dispersed coherently within an FCC FeCoNi matrix.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Compositional and lattice mismatch around the precipitates creates regions of increased magnetic anisotropy.
The increased local magnetic anisotropy impedes domain-wall motion and thereby raises coercivity.
Formation of an ordered, multiphase microstructure can be associated with increased coercivity.
The annealed FeCoNi alloy will have coercivity significantly above 100 Oe and approximately twofold or more above the single-phase FCC baseline.
The coercivity increase will occur with only a minimal reduction in saturation magnetization.
The intervention is effective only when precipitation remains limited and extensive phase decomposition is avoided.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement depends on precipitate size, volume fraction, distribution, and coherence with the matrix.

contradictions.description: The prediction defines a twofold increase relative to a baseline that may be anywhere at or below 100 Oe, whereas the falsification rule says 'a twofold increase above 100 Oe.' These are not equivalent when the matched baseline is substantially below 100 Oe.
